facts: Saw that the time for positive action had come

Believes there's a chance of putting the thing out of business
Has seen Wilbur Whateley's diary
Has read some of the strange old books Wilbur Whateley used to read

sources.quote: Armitage saw that the time for positive action had come, and spoke decisively to the faltering group of frightened rustics.
I've seen Wilbur Whateley's diary and read some of the strange old books he used to read, and I think I know the right kind of a spell to recite to make the thing fade away.
It's invisible—I knew it would be—but there's a powder in this long-distance sprayer that might make it show up for a second.
When Armitage inadvertently took a wrong direction, Joe Osborn warned him and walked ahead to show the right one.
Armitage produced a pocket telescope of considerable power and scanned the steep green side of the hill. Then he handed the instrument to Morgan, whose sight was keener.

name: Wilbur Whateley
facts: Kept a diary that Armitage has seen
Read strange old books
Would have let in something worse than the current thing if he had lived longer
fate: Implied to no longer be alive, as referenced in the past tense regarding what he would have done 'if he'd lived longer'

sources.quote: I've seen Wilbur Whateley's diary and read some of the strange old books he used to read, and I think I know the right kind of a spell to recite to make the thing fade away.
It's a frightful thing to have alive, but it isn't as bad as what Wilbur would have let in if he'd lived longer.

name: Rice
facts: Walked with Armitage and Morgan toward the wrecked place, in the direction indicated by Earl Sawyer

sources.quote: Armitage, with Rice and Morgan, started to walk in the direction indicated; and most of the natives followed slowly.

name: Morgan
facts: Walked with Armitage and Rice toward the wrecked place
Had keener sight than Armitage

Passed the telescope to Earl Sawyer, indicating a spot on the slope

sources.quote: Armitage, with Rice and Morgan, started to walk in the direction indicated; and most of the natives followed slowly.

Then he handed the instrument to Morgan, whose sight was keener. After a moment of gazing Morgan cried out sharply, passing the glass to Earl Sawyer and indicating a certain spot on the slope with his finger.

name: Earl Sawyer
facts: Spoke softly, pointing with a grimy finger through the lessening rain
Gave directions to reach Seth Bishop's place by cutting across the lower meadow, wading the brook, and climbing through Carrier's mowing and the timber-lot
Received the telescope from Morgan and fumbled before focusing it with Armitage's aid
Cried out that the grass and bushes on the hill were moving, creeping up toward the top

sources.quote: The men shuffled about a moment, and then Earl Sawyer spoke softly, pointing with a grimy finger through the steadily lessening rain.
I guess ye kin git to Seth Bishop's quickest by cuttin' acrost the lower medder here, wadin' the brook at the low place, an' climbin' through Carrier's mowin' an' the timber-lot beyont.
Sawyer, as clumsy as most non-users of optical devices are, fumbled a while; but eventually focused the lenses with Armitage's aid.
Gawd almighty, the grass an' bushes is a-movin'! It's a-goin' up—slow-like—creepin' up ter the top this minute, heaven only knows what fer!

facts: Was a gathering point where able-bodied men-folk were rounded up with Fords and wagons

sources.quote: We that heerd it got aout Fords an' wagons an' raounded up as many able-bodied men-folks as we could get, at Corey's place, an' come up here ter see what yew thought best ter dew.

They were a little beyond the Seth Bishop place, but bent trees and hideously unmistakable tracks showed what had passed by. Only a few moments were consumed in surveying the ruins just around the bend. It was the Frye incident all over again, and nothing dead or living was found in either of the collapsed shells which had been the Bishop house and barn.
